title: Partnering with an Indian Corporate Travel Company: A Guide for DMCs
excerpt: What destination management companies gain from partnering with an Indian corporate travel company, what that partner will expect, and how to begin.
meta: What destination management companies gain from partnering with an Indian corporate travel company, what that partner will expect, and how to begin.

body.p: Destination management companies are the people who make a trip work on the ground. Airport transfers, local transport, venues, guides, group logistics: the parts of a journey a traveller only notices when they go wrong. For a DMC that chooses to partner directly with an Indian travel company, that partner can be a steady source of exactly this work.

body.h2: The work Indian companies send abroad

body.p: Indian companies travel for more than meetings. They run conferences and offsites overseas, reward their top performers with incentive trips, and move teams to project sites for months at a time. Each of these needs someone local: a partner who knows the venues, the drivers and the rules.

At Elyra, MICE and corporate events, chauffeur-driven ground transport and corporate holidays sit alongside hotels and serviced apartments as core services. When a client’s event or group trip lands in a city where we do not have our own people, a local DMC is how we deliver it.

body.h2: What a corporate travel partner expects from a DMC

body.p: Reliability over novelty. Corporate groups are judged by their employer, not by the itinerary. A DMC that delivers the plan exactly, every time, is worth more than one with clever ideas and loose execution.
Clear quotes, early. Events are budgeted and approved inside companies before anything is booked. Partners who quote promptly and itemise clearly make that approval easier.
One point of contact. When something changes on the day, the travel company needs a single person who can act.
Duty of care. Companies are responsible for their employees abroad. Vetted drivers, sound venues and a plan for when things go wrong are part of the job.
Clean billing. Invoices need to match what was agreed and arrive in a form a finance team can reconcile.

body.h2: What a DMC gains

body.p: Repeat demand. Companies that hold an offsite in a city one year often return, and a travel company that trusted a DMC once will use it again.
Business you could not reach alone. Indian companies rarely go looking for a DMC abroad themselves. They ask their travel partner, and the travel partner calls the DMCs it knows.
A direct line. Working with the travel company itself, rather than through further intermediaries, keeps terms clear and communication short.

body.h2: Where to start

body.p: If you are a destination management company and want to work with corporate groups from India, tell us about your business on our partnerships page. Elyra has served 150+ corporate clients since 2016, across 185+ countries, and our team in Mumbai will be in touch.

faq: Why would an Indian corporate travel company work with a DMC?
For events, group travel and ground arrangements in cities where it has no team of its own. The DMC provides local knowledge and execution, and the travel company provides the client relationship.
What should a DMC have in place before approaching a corporate travel partner?
Clear itemised pricing, a single responsive point of contact, vetted suppliers, and invoicing that a corporate finance team can reconcile.

title: How Overseas Hotels and Serviced Apartments Can Win Indian Corporate Travellers
excerpt: How hotels and serviced apartments outside India can reach corporate travellers from India, what travel management companies look for, and where to start.
meta: How hotels and serviced apartments outside India can reach corporate travellers from India, what travel management companies look for, and where to start.

body.p: Indian companies send people abroad constantly: consultants to client sites, engineers to project launches, managers on secondment, employees relocating with their families. For a hotel or serviced apartment in London, Frankfurt or Singapore, these are valuable guests. They travel on company budgets, they often stay longer than a leisure guest, and the same company sends the next traveller to the same city a few weeks later.

The difficulty for a property outside India is reach. Most of these trips are never booked by the traveller alone, which means the property that wins them is rarely the one with the best listing. It is the one the company’s travel partner already knows, because it holds a direct contract with a travel management company.

body.h2: How these bookings are actually made

body.p: A large Indian company does not let every employee book wherever they like. It writes a travel policy that sets budgets, preferred suppliers and approval rules, and it hands the work to a travel management company. That company books through a managed desk, through a self-booking platform the employees use themselves, or through both.

At Elyra, for example, a trip reaches a property in one of two ways: our desk books it on the traveller’s behalf, or the employee books it on Travgenie, our corporate self-booking platform, within their company’s policy. In both cases, the options the traveller sees are shaped by the properties we have relationships with.
So the question for an overseas property is not how to get Indian travellers to find you. It is how to be one of the properties their travel company offers.

body.h2: What a travel management company looks for

body.p: Location that matches the work. Corporate travellers go where the offices, client sites and project locations are. A property ten minutes from a business district will usually beat a better-rated one across town.

Stays that work for weeks. Project and relocation travellers need a kitchen, laundry, a proper desk and reliable internet. Serviced apartments win much of this business because a hotel room is hard to live in for a month.
Predictable terms. A travel company commits its clients to your property. It needs rates, cancellation rules and availability that hold, so it can quote with confidence.
Clear billing. Corporate travel runs on invoices that a finance team can reconcile. Properties that bill accurately and on time are easier to keep sending people to.
Responsiveness. When a flight is delayed or a project is extended, the travel company needs a person at the property who answers.

body.h2: Why a direct contract beats waiting to be found

body.p: Online travel agencies give a property visibility, but visibility is not the same as being chosen. A corporate traveller booking within policy sees a shortlist, and that shortlist comes from the travel company’s own relationships.

A direct contract changes your position. Instead of hoping a traveller scrolls to your listing, a team that books thousands of corporate stays is actively offering your property to the companies it serves. You agree the rate and terms once, and the bookings follow the travel patterns of those companies.
It also removes layers. Every intermediary between your property and the guest takes margin and adds a step where information can be lost.

body.h2: You do not need an office in India

body.p: Many overseas properties assume that winning Indian corporate business means hiring sales staff in Mumbai or Bengaluru. It does not. A travel management company based in India already sells to those companies every day. Partnering with one gives you that reach without the cost of building it.

body.h2: Where to start

body.p: If you run a hotel, serviced apartment or aparthotel and want to host corporate travellers from India, the simplest first step is a conversation. Elyra has placed travellers from 150+ corporate clients across 185+ countries since 2016, and we are expanding the properties we contract with directly.
Tell us about your property on our partnerships page, and our team in Mumbai will be in touch.

faq: Do Indian companies book hotels abroad directly?

Larger companies usually do not. They set a travel policy and use a travel management company, which books through a managed desk or a self-booking platform. The properties offered to travellers come from that company's relationships.
What do corporate travellers from India need from a serviced apartment?
Long-stay essentials: a kitchen, laundry, a proper workspace and reliable internet, in a location close to where they are working. Project and relocation stays can run for weeks.
How can a hotel outside India reach Indian corporate travellers?

By contracting with a travel management company that already serves Indian companies. The travel company represents the property to its clients, so the property reaches that market without opening an office in India.

title: Corporate Housing vs Hotel: Which Is Better for Your Long-Term Business Stays?
excerpt: Corporate housing or a hotel for a long business stay? Compare the benefits, limits and costs of each, and when each one suits your team.
meta: Corporate housing or a hotel for a long business stay? Compare the benefits, limits and costs of each, and when each one suits your team.

body.p: Did you know that 69% of corporate travel buyers identify rising travel costs as a major influence on their travel planning? According to the Global Business Travel Association’s September 2026 survey, managing expenses remains a priority for businesses worldwide.

But cost is only one part of the decision. When employees travel for weeks or months, comfort, convenience, and everyday facilities matter equally. Should you choose a business hotel with professional hospitality services or corporate housing with residential comforts? Understanding the benefits, practical considerations, and overall costs of both helps you choose accommodation that genuinely suits your employees and business.

A senior executive visiting Dubai for important meetings may appreciate the convenience of a hotel. An employee relocating to Singapore for three months may prefer the independence of an apartment. A project team travelling to Mumbai might have entirely different requirements.
That’s why the Corporate Housing vs Hotel comparison deserves a closer look.

img.alt: Furnished corporate housing for long-term business stays.

body.p: Both are valuable forms of business travel accommodation. Understanding what each offers helps HR managers, travel administrators, and corporate decision-makers arrange comfortable stays while managing company budgets.

body.h2: What Is Corporate Housing, and How Is It Different from a Hotel?

body.quote: Corporate housing is furnished residential accommodation designed for temporary business stays, while hotels provide professionally managed rooms and hospitality services for short or extended visits.

body.p: Both can offer comfortable accommodation, but the experience and facilities may differ.
Corporate housing: Usually includes furnished apartments or residences with separate living, sleeping, and cooking areas. These properties often suit employees who prefer a residential routine.
Business hotels: Offer furnished rooms supported by hospitality services such as reception, housekeeping, dining facilities and other amenities, depending on the property category.
Serviced apartments: Combine residential facilities with selected professional services, making them a practical form of extended stay accommodation.
Hotel suites and extended-stay hotels: Can provide additional space, kitchenettes and other facilities, depending on the hotel.

body.h3: Corporate Housing vs Hotel: A Side-by-Side Comparison

body.p: The important point is that neither category has identical facilities across every property. Always compare actual inclusions before confirming a booking.

table: Suitable for short and extended stays
Usually separate living and sleeping areas
Available in selected rooms or suites
On-site restaurants and room service at selected properties
Desks or dedicated work areas in selected properties

body.h2: What Are the Benefits and Limitations of Hotels for Long Business Stays?

body.quote: Business hotels offer convenience, professional hospitality services and a range of accommodation categories that can suit employees travelling for meetings, projects and extended assignments.

img.alt: Business hotel room for corporate travelers on extended stays

body.p: Here is where hotels can be particularly useful.
Convenient services: Many business hotels provide reception assistance, housekeeping, dining and concierge support. Employees can access everyday services without making separate arrangements.
Location advantages: Hotels are often located near airports, commercial districts, convention centres and major transport routes. This can be valuable for employees with packed schedules.
Accommodation choices: From budget and business hotels to premium and executive properties, companies can select rooms according to employee roles, preferences and travel budgets.
Business facilities: Selected hotels offer meeting rooms, conference facilities, business centres, restaurants and other amenities that support corporate travellers.
Booking flexibility: Depending on the property and negotiated rate, hotels may offer practical options for changing arrival dates, departure dates or room categories.

body.h3: What should you consider before booking a hotel for several months?

body.p: Room configuration: Standard rooms may provide less separation between work and relaxation. Executive rooms, suites or extended-stay hotels can offer additional space.
Meal arrangements: Travellers who prefer preparing their own food should check whether kitchen or kitchenette facilities are available.
Overall expenses: Room rates, dining, laundry and other services should be compared together, particularly for longer assignments.
Employee preferences: Some employees enjoy access to hotel facilities throughout their stay, while others prefer a residential environment.
A hotel can remain an excellent choice for a longer assignment when its facilities, location and services match the traveller’s needs.

body.h2: What Are the Benefits and Limitations of Corporate Housing for Extended Business Stays?

body.p: Long-term corporate housing offers furnished living spaces and everyday facilities that can support employees staying away from home for several weeks or months.
The benefits often relate to how employees manage their daily routines.

Space for everyday living: Many corporate apartments provide separate areas for sleeping, relaxing and working. This arrangement can be convenient when an employee spends several weeks in the same city.
Cooking facilities: A kitchen gives travellers the flexibility to prepare meals according to their schedules, preferences and dietary needs.
Residential comfort: Furnished living areas, storage, laundry facilities and household amenities can help employees settle into a temporary routine.
Suitable for relocating families: Employees travelling with spouses or children may appreciate additional bedrooms, living space and access to neighbourhood facilities.
Longer stay arrangements: Some corporate apartment rentals offer weekly or monthly pricing, which companies can compare against negotiated hotel rates.

body.h3: What should you check before choosing a serviced apartment?

body.p: Housekeeping frequency: Service schedules differ between properties, so confirm what is included.
On-site assistance: Some apartments have reception or concierge services, while others provide support through property management teams.
Dining preferences: Travellers who enjoy restaurant dining or room service should check the available options nearby or within the property.
Minimum stay conditions: Certain properties have booking requirements, cancellation terms, or extension policies that should be reviewed in advance.
Location and connectivity: Check commuting distance, transport availability, and access to everyday essentials.
These considerations help companies evaluate furnished corporate housing according to actual employee requirements.

body.h2: Is Corporate Housing or a Hotel More Cost-Effective for Long Business Stays?

body.p: Both corporate housing and hotels can offer cost-effective arrangements for extended assignments, depending on negotiated rates, included services, location, and employee preferences.
The best comparison considers the total cost of the stay rather than the accommodation rate alone.
Accommodation charges: Hotels may offer negotiated corporate rates, while serviced apartments may have weekly or monthly pricing. Request quotations for the same dates before comparing.

Meals and dining: Hotels with breakfast packages or dining arrangements can be convenient for busy employees. Apartments with kitchens offer flexibility for those who prefer preparing their own meals.
Housekeeping and laundry: Check which services are included and whether additional charges apply. Both accommodation categories can offer managed services.
Commuting expenses: A conveniently located property may provide better overall value, even when its accommodation rate is slightly higher.
Booking conditions: Compare cancellation policies, extension charges, deposits, and minimum stay requirements.

body.h2: When Should Companies Choose Corporate Housing, and When Is a Hotel Better?

body.p: The right corporate accommodation depends on the purpose of the trip, the employee’s preferred routine, the length of the assignment, and the facilities required.
Here are some common business travel situations.

table: Depends on preferred services, space and routine
Senior executive on an extended assignment
Executive hotel suite or premium serviced apartment
Project team working across multiple cities
Different locations and durations may require different solutions

body.p: There is no fixed rule that an assignment lasting 15, 30 or 90 days must use a particular accommodation type.
A traveller staying for two months may still prefer a hotel. Another staying for three weeks may find an apartment more convenient.
The best accommodation is the one that matches the traveller’s requirements, rather than simply the number of nights.

body.quote: Elyra helps companies arrange both corporate hotels and serviced apartments across India and international destinations, based on traveller requirements, budgets, locations, and assignment durations.

body.p: Elyra works with businesses that need accommodation for individual employees, senior executives, relocating families, and project teams.
Its services include:

Serviced apartments: Companies can access furnished apartments suited to short, medium and extended assignments, with property selection based on location, facilities and budget. Explore Elyra Serviced Apartments.

Corporate booking coordination: Property shortlisting, rate negotiation, billing arrangements and ongoing assistance can help travel managers coordinate accommodation across different destinations.
Connected travel services: Companies can also explore Elyra Corporate Travel Services for ground transport, employee relocation and other business travel requirements.
This gives businesses the flexibility to consider hotels and serviced apartments within the same corporate travel programme.

body.h2: Final Thoughts: The Right Stay Depends on the Right Requirements

body.p: Choosing between corporate housing and hotels is about understanding what will make an employee’s business trip comfortable, convenient and practical.

Hotels offer professional hospitality, dining and business facilities. Serviced apartments offer residential space and flexibility for everyday living. Both can support successful extended assignments when chosen carefully.

What should companies ask corporate housing providers before booking?

title: How to Choose the Right Corporate Stay for Your Business
excerpt: A practical guide to corporate stays: what to consider, hotel or serviced apartment, managing accommodation costs, and when a travel partner helps.
meta: A practical guide to corporate stays: what to consider, hotel or serviced apartment, managing accommodation costs, and when a travel partner helps.

body.p: Managing business travel for multiple employees? Then you know how challenging it can be to find accommodation that fits everyone’s schedule, preferences, and company budget. A hotel may suit an executive attending meetings in Dubai, while a serviced apartment may work better for an employee on a three-month assignment in London.

That’s where Elyra makes the process easier. With access to hotels, serviced apartments, and corporate accommodation across India and worldwide, Elyra helps businesses find stays that match their requirements.
But how do you choose the right corporate stay? Let’s explore what really matters before booking.

body.h2: What Should You Consider Before Booking a Corporate Stay?

body.quote: The right corporate stay depends on five essentials: trip duration, employee requirements, location, available facilities, and the company’s overall accommodation budget.

body.p: Before you begin comparing properties, understand what your employees actually need.

Purpose of travel: An executive attending client meetings may prioritise a central hotel with convenient services. A project employee staying for several weeks may prefer a furnished apartment with a kitchen and living area.
Length of assignment: A two-night visit, a three-week training programme and a six-month relocation involve different routines. Match the accommodation to the expected duration.
Traveller preferences: Consider who is travelling. A senior executive, individual employee, project team, or relocating family may have different expectations for space, privacy, and amenities.
Location and accessibility: Check commuting distances to offices, industrial sites and meeting venues. Nearby transport, restaurants and everyday essentials also matter.
Total budget: Compare accommodation charges alongside meals, laundry, local travel, taxes and additional services. This gives you a clearer picture of the actual expense.
These details help you shortlist suitable business travel accommodation rather than selecting properties based on photographs or room rates alone.

body.h2: Should You Choose a Business Hotel or a Serviced Apartment?

body.quote: Hotels offer professional hospitality and convenient services, while serviced apartments provide residential facilities and additional living space. Both can suit business travellers.

body.p: Your decision should reflect how employees will spend their time during the assignment.

img.alt: Business hotel room for corporate travelers on extended stays

table: Standard, premium, executive rooms and suites
Hotel restaurants and room service, where available
In-room desks and selected business facilities
Connecting rooms or suites, where available

body.p: When hotels work well: A hotel can be convenient for employees with busy meeting schedules, frequent travel changes or a preference for reception, dining and hospitality services.
When apartments work well: Corporate stay apartments may suit employees who prefer cooking, additional living space and an everyday residential routine during longer assignments.

When both are suitable: A six-week assignment may work equally well in an executive hotel suite or a premium serviced apartment. The final choice depends on facilities, location, price, and traveller preferences.
Companies can explore Elyra corporate hotel booking options and serviced apartments for business travellers to compare accommodation types.

body.h2: How Can Companies Manage Corporate Accommodation Costs Effectively?

body.p: Managing corporate accommodation costs involves comparing complete stay expenses, negotiating suitable rates and choosing properties that match employee requirements.
A practical cost review should cover the following.
Compare total stay prices: Request quotations for the full assignment rather than comparing nightly rates alone. Hotels and apartments may offer different corporate pricing structures.
Review included facilities: Breakfast, housekeeping, WiFi, laundry, utilities, and parking can affect the overall cost. Check what is included in each quotation.
Consider commuting expenses: A property close to the workplace may reduce transport costs and make daily schedules easier.
Plan for possible extensions: Project dates can change. Review cancellation terms, additional night charges and extension arrangements before booking.
Coordinate group requirements: When several employees travel together, compare room categories, apartment configurations and group booking arrangements.
Maintain billing visibility: Centralised invoices, approval processes and clear expense records can simplify corporate travel management for finance and administration teams.
The most suitable property is not necessarily the one with the lowest advertised rate. It is the one that offers the right combination of facilities, services and overall value.

body.h2: How Can You Choose Accommodation That Supports Employee Comfort and Productivity?

body.p: Suitable employee accommodation should help travellers follow their work schedules comfortably while giving them access to the facilities and support they need.
Employee experience deserves as much attention as pricing.
Comfortable surroundings: Check room size, bedding, lighting, ventilation, and noise levels. A well-maintained room or apartment can make a difference after a busy working day.
Practical work facilities: Employees attending online meetings may need dependable WiFi and a proper desk. Confirm these facilities before booking.
Dining preferences: Some travellers appreciate hotel restaurants and breakfast services. Others prefer apartments where they can prepare their own meals.
Safety and assistance: Review property security, reception availability, emergency contacts, and support arrangements, especially for international assignments.
Everyday convenience: Laundry, housekeeping, nearby supermarkets and transport connections become increasingly important during long-term business accommodation.

A useful approach is to ask employees about their essential requirements before booking. This helps you select accommodation for business travellers that supports both professional responsibilities and personal comfort.

body.h2: When Should You Work with a Corporate Travel Management Company?

body.quote: A corporate travel management company can help businesses compare accommodation options, negotiate rates, coordinate bookings, and manage employee stays across multiple destinations.

body.p: This becomes particularly useful when companies have frequent or complex travel requirements.

Access to different accommodation types: A suitable corporate accommodation provider can offer business hotels, executive rooms, serviced apartments, and corporate housing, allowing companies to choose according to the assignment.
Support across destinations: When employees travel to Mumbai, London, Singapore, Amsterdam or Dubai, a single corporate travel company can help coordinate requirements across locations.
Booking and approval processes: Structured corporate travel management services can help ensure bookings follow company policies and authorised budgets.
Billing coordination: Consolidated invoices and clear payment arrangements can simplify financial reporting for travel and finance departments.
Assistance during assignments: Changes to project schedules, accommodation extensions, and unexpected requirements may need ongoing coordination.
Technology and reporting: Digital booking systems can help administrators monitor reservations, approvals and travel spending.
For companies managing regular travel, these capabilities make it easier to organise corporate lodging across different employees, departments and locations.

body.quote: Elyra helps companies arrange hotels and serviced apartments worldwide, with accommodation selected according to travel duration, employee preferences, location and budget.

body.p: Established in 2016, Elyra supports corporate clients with stays across India and international business destinations. We pride ourselves on having a network spanning 185+ countries and over 700,000 properties.
Our corporate accommodation services include:

Serviced apartments: Businesses can explore global serviced apartment options for extended assignments, relocations and project teams requiring furnished living spaces.
Ground transport: Employees can arrange chauffeur-driven transport and airport transfers alongside their accommodation requirements.
Centralised booking: We support company travel policies, approval workflows and spending visibility.
Coordinated assistance: Elyra supports property selection, negotiated rates, flexible billing and ongoing accommodation requirements.
Companies can use these corporate travel solutions individually or combine them according to their travel programme.

body.h3: Choose the Stay That Works for Your Business

body.p: The right corporate stay begins with understanding your employees, their assignments, and your company’s priorities.

Hotels offer convenient hospitality services, while serviced apartments provide residential facilities and flexible living arrangements. Both can deliver a comfortable business travel experience when selected thoughtfully.
Before your next booking, compare location, facilities, overall cost and traveller preferences.
If your team travels regularly, explore Elyra corporate travel services to find accommodation options suited to your business requirements.

title: When Is the Best Time to Book an Umrah Package from India? November 2026 to Ramadan 2027
excerpt: November, December, January or Ramadan? How to pick the right time for Umrah from India in 2026 and 2027, and when to book for each.
meta: November, December, January or Ramadan? How to pick the right time for Umrah from India in 2026 and 2027, and when to book for each.

body.p: Planning Umrah with your family but unsure when to book? You may be considering the November holidays, a December winter break, or a peaceful journey in January 2027. But finding suitable hotels near the Haram, coordinating family requirements, and choosing comfortable transfers can take time, especially around popular travel periods.

img.alt: Pilgrims at Masjid al-Haram in Makkah for Umrah

body.p: Elyra (Elyra Holidays) helps you plan a customised Umrah Package around your preferred dates, budget, hotel category, and group size. With flexible stays, private transfers, and guided Ziyarat, you can organise the journey around your needs.
So, which month should you choose, and how early should you begin?

body.h2: When Is the Best Time to Book an Umrah Package from India in 2026–27?

body.p: The best time to book an Umrah Package from India depends on your preferred month, family schedule, hotel availability, and budget, with earlier planning particularly useful around holidays and Ramadan.
If you are planning to travel within the next few months, these periods deserve consideration.

table: Families, couples and travellers seeking a pre-winter journey
Families using Christmas and winter holidays
Compare hotels and dates as early as possible
Working professionals and families preferring a post-holiday trip
Begin planning in October or November 2026, if possible
Check official seasonal deadlines before planning

body.p: These are suggested planning windows, not confirmed availability or guaranteed lower-price periods.

November 2026: November can be a practical choice when your family has some flexibility before the December holiday period. You can compare hotel categories, stay durations, and guided Ziyarat arrangements without having to follow a fixed group departure.

December 2026: Christmas holidays and winter vacations make December convenient for families with school-going children and working professionals using year-end leave. Because these dates are popular for international travel, early accommodation enquiries are sensible.

January 2027: January may appeal to travellers who prefer scheduling their pilgrimage after the year-end holiday period. It is also worth considering if you need time to coordinate leave, family members and hotel preferences.

Ramadan 2027: Ramadan is expected to run from approximately 8 February to 8 March 2027, subject to moon sighting. If this is your preferred period, begin planning well in advance, particularly when travelling with elderly parents or a larger family.

body.h2: Is November, December or January Better for an Umrah Trip from Mumbai?

body.p: November, December and January can all be suitable for an Umrah trip from Mumbai, but the best month depends on your available leave, preferred experience and accommodation budget.
Each month has a different practical advantage.

November vacation: This can work for travellers who have flexible leave or want to complete their journey before the December holiday season. Compare accommodation locations and transport arrangements early.

Christmas holidays in December: Families can use school breaks and annual leave to plan their pilgrimage together. Hotels near the Haram may attract greater interest during popular holiday dates, so availability should be checked before finalising plans.

January winter vacation: January offers another opportunity to plan around work and family schedules. Saudi Arabia generally experiences milder winter weather than the peak summer months, although conditions differ between Makkah and Madinah.
Travelling with elderly parents: Whichever month you choose, prioritise hotel distance from the Haram, accessible rooms, manageable walking distances and comfortable ground transport.
Travelling with children: Consider family room arrangements, meal preferences and enough time for rest between activities.
When comparing Umrah packages from Mumbai, choose dates that allow your family to travel comfortably rather than selecting a month solely because it appears popular.

body.h2: When Should You Book Umrah Packages for Ramadan 2027?

body.p: Travellers planning Ramadan Umrah in 2027 should begin comparing accommodation and transport options several months ahead, particularly for family stays and preferred hotels near the Haram.
Ramadan is a deeply meaningful period for many pilgrims, and the journey deserves careful preparation.
Expected Ramadan dates: Ramadan 1448 AH is expected to begin around 8 February 2027 and conclude around 8 March 2027. Final dates depend on official moon sighting.

October and November 2026 enquiries: These months offer a useful planning opportunity for travellers considering Ramadan umrah packages, especially when preferred hotel locations or multiple rooms are important.
First half or final ten nights: Decide which part of Ramadan matters most to you. Hotel demand, room availability, and local conditions can differ significantly across the month.
Family requirements: If travelling with children or elderly relatives, consider nearby hotels, private transfers, rest periods and manageable itineraries.

Official Umrah deadlines: Saudi Arabia’s Ministry of Hajj and Umrah has announced 9 March 2027 as the last date for issuing Umrah visas, 23 March as the final entry date for Umrah visa holders, and 7 April as the final departure deadline for those pilgrims under the 1448 AH season calendar.
These dates make it particularly important to verify entry eligibility and current travel rules before confirming late-season plans.
You can review the official announcement from the Saudi Press Agency.

body.h3: How Can You Choose an Umrah Package That Matches Your Budget and Family?

body.p: The right Umrah Package combines suitable accommodation, a comfortable itinerary, dependable ground transport, and a duration that fits your family, without unnecessary services or expenses.
Before comparing Umrah packages from Mumbai price quotations, look at what each arrangement includes.
Hotel location: A hotel closer to the Haram may be convenient, particularly for elderly pilgrims. Compare walking distances, accessibility, and room facilities.
Stay duration: A shorter umrah tour package may suit working professionals, while families may prefer 10 to 15 days to spend more time in Makkah and Madinah.
Room preferences: An Umrah package for family should account for the number of travellers, children’s ages, connecting rooms and any accessibility requirements.
Comfort level: A luxury umrah package may include premium hotels and private ground arrangements. Comfortable alternatives can also be planned around different budgets.
Group requirements: A group umrah package can be useful for extended families or community groups, particularly when rooms and ground transport need to be coordinated together.

title: How to Reduce Corporate Travel Costs Without Cutting Quality
excerpt: Seven levers that lower travel spend without cutting trips or pushing everyone down a tier — and three popular savings that cost more than they save.
meta: Seven levers that lower travel spend without cutting trips or pushing everyone down a tier — and three popular savings that cost more than they save.

body.p: Travel is usually one of the larger controllable line items in a business, which makes it a standing target whenever budgets tighten. The reflex is to cut trips or push everyone down a tier. Both work, briefly, and both have costs that show up somewhere else. There is a longer list of savings that do not degrade the trip, and most programmes have not worked through it.

body.h2: First, find out what you actually spend

body.p: Most companies know their air and hotel spend and underestimate the total, because ground transport, booking fees and the expense-claim tail sit in different places. Before optimising anything, get one number that includes all of it for a full year. It is common for the parts nobody was tracking to be the parts with the most slack in them — and hotel programmes in particular reward attention, which is why corporate hotel booking is usually the first place to look.

body.h2: Seven levers, roughly in order of return

body.h3: 1. Put every booking through one channel

body.p: This is the precondition for everything else. Spend that is scattered across personal cards and consumer sites cannot be negotiated with, reported on, or used to find someone in a crisis. Consolidating typically produces a saving on its own, purely by making volume visible to suppliers — and it makes every lever below possible.

body.h3: 2. Negotiate on your real pattern, not a generic one

body.p: Rate negotiations go better when you can show a supplier exactly what you bring: nights per year in their city, typical length of stay, day-of-week distribution, how far ahead you book. A programme that can evidence sixty predictable nights a year in one property is negotiating from a different position than one that cannot.

The corollary is that a rate card negotiated once and rolled over annually stops reflecting reality fairly quickly. Travel patterns shift as offices open, clients change and projects move. It is worth re-running the exercise each year against the previous twelve months of actual bookings rather than against last year’s assumptions.

body.h3: 3. Match the accommodation format to the length of stay

body.p: For stays past roughly a week, a serviced apartment is often cheaper fully loaded than a hotel — lower nightly rate on a longer let, and a kitchen that removes most of the food and laundry spend around it. Programmes that default to hotels for everything leave this on the table for exactly the longest, most expensive trips.

body.h3: 4. Book earlier by making it easier to book earlier

body.p: Last-minute booking is expensive and almost never a genuine emergency; it is usually a slow approval chain or an unclear policy. Shortening the approval path is a cost lever disguised as a process improvement.

body.h3: 5. Take the incidentals seriously

body.p: Breakfast, wifi, parking, laundry, airport transfers and late checkout are individually trivial and collectively material. Negotiating them into the rate is often easier than negotiating the rate, because it costs the supplier less.

body.h3: 6. Buy ground transport deliberately

body.p: Ground transport is where policies are vaguest and spend leaks quietly. A pre-booked transfer at a contracted rate is usually cheaper than the same journey expensed at whatever the app charged at the time, and it is easier to reconcile. Surge pricing on an airport run at the wrong hour can cost several times the contracted equivalent, and it lands as an expense claim nobody queries.

The same applies to longer deployments. A team of engineers on site for two months taking individual taxis every day is a materially different cost from a single arranged vehicle, and nobody notices the difference until someone totals the expense claims at the end of the quarter.

body.h3: 7. Review the exceptions every quarter

body.p: Exceptions are the most honest data in a programme. A recurring exception is not misbehaviour — it is a rule that does not fit the business. Fixing the rule is free.

body.h2: Three savings that cost more than they save

body.h3: Cutting the trip that was going to close the deal

body.p: Travel is not uniformly discretionary. A blanket freeze treats a renewal visit and an internal workshop as the same thing. Segment by purpose before cutting by percentage.

body.h3: Downgrading the long-haul overnight before a working day

body.p: Somebody who lands unable to function has cost more in a wasted day than the fare difference saved. This is a narrow case and worth protecting explicitly in policy so it is not re-argued every time.

body.h3: Making people book it themselves

body.p: Removing support looks free because the cost moves onto people whose time is not charged to travel. A senior person spending forty minutes comparing flights is not a saving, and the trip they book is usually worse.

body.h2: Two things worth measuring while you do it

body.h3: Savings against what, exactly

body.p: A negotiated rate that is lower than rack rate is not a saving if nobody was paying rack rate. Measure against what the company actually paid for comparable trips last year, not against a published price. It is a less flattering number and the only one worth reporting twice.

body.h3: The cost of the process itself

body.p: Every control has an administrative price: approvals to chase, exceptions to adjudicate, claims to check. If a policy change saves a modest amount per trip and adds ten minutes of somebody’s time to every booking, it is worth working out which side of that trade you are on before rolling it out.

body.h2: What good looks like after a year

list: Most trips booked through one channel, early enough to get sensible pricing.
Rates negotiated against evidence, reviewed annually rather than rolled over.
Accommodation format chosen by trip length instead of by habit.
Ground transport contracted rather than expensed.
A short exceptions list that gets shorter because the policy keeps absorbing it.

body.p: None of that requires anyone to fly less or stay somewhere worse. It requires the programme to be visible enough to manage, which is usually the actual problem.

title: Serviced Apartments vs Hotels for Business Travel
excerpt: Not which format is better — how to tell which one a given trip needs. Where the cost lines actually cross, the five factors that decide it, and where a hotel still wins outright.
meta: Not which format is better — how to tell which one a given trip needs. Where the cost lines actually cross, the five factors that decide it, and where a…

body.p: Most accommodation decisions in a corporate programme are made one booking at a time, by whoever is making the booking, against whatever is available. That works until somebody asks why a twelve-week posting was billed as eighty-four separate hotel nights. This is a way of running the comparison properly — not which format is better, but how to tell which one a given trip needs.

body.h2: The two formats, briefly

body.p: A hotel sells you a room by the night, staffed, with a front desk and a food operation attached. A serviced apartment lets you a self-contained home — bedroom, living space, an equipped kitchen — with housekeeping, utilities and internet folded into one rate, usually on a minimum stay of a few nights or more.

The formats blur at the edges. Aparthotels have receptions and look like hotels from the lobby. Extended-stay brands sit in between. If you want the underlying distinction and where each format sits, we have written about serviced apartments for corporate stays separately; this piece assumes you know roughly what they are and want to decide between them.

body.h2: Where the cost lines cross

body.p: The honest answer is that it depends on the length of stay, and that the crossover is closer than most programmes assume.

body.h3: A nightly rate is not the whole cost

body.p: A hotel rate covers the room. Around it sit breakfast if it is not included, dinner most nights because there is no kitchen, laundry at per-item hotel pricing, and whatever the minibar and the parking add. None of that appears in the rate you negotiated, and all of it appears on an expense claim later.

An apartment rate covers the home. Utilities, internet, housekeeping at an agreed frequency and often parking are inside it. The traveller can cook, so food spend drops toward what they would spend at home. The rate looks higher per night against a budget hotel and frequently lower once the surrounding spend is counted.

body.h3: So compare the total, not the rate

body.p: The comparison worth running is the fully loaded cost of the whole stay: accommodation plus expected meals, laundry, transport to the office and any incidental the format forces. Do it for one real trip you have already paid for and you will usually find the crossover sits somewhere between one and two weeks — earlier in expensive cities, later where hotel supply is cheap.

body.h2: Five factors that decide it

body.h3: 1. How long, honestly

body.p: Not the length on the project plan — the length it will actually run to. Assignments extend. If there is a realistic chance of a four-week posting becoming ten, the apartment case starts earlier than the plan suggests.

body.h3: 2. Where the work is

body.p: Hotels cluster in city centres and near airports. Work does not always. An apartment fifteen minutes from a plant or a client site is worth more to the person staying there than a better-known address forty minutes away in traffic.

body.h3: 3. What the traveller is doing all day

body.p: Somebody in back-to-back meetings for two nights wants a desk, a shower and breakfast at seven. Somebody running a three-month integration wants a kitchen, a washing machine and somewhere to sit that is not the end of a bed. These are different products and the trip type, not a house preference, should pick between them.

body.h3: 4. How it needs to be billed

body.p: A single monthly invoice for a long let reconciles very differently from ninety nightly charges spread over two quarters. If your programme runs on cost-centre allocation or centralised billing, that difference is often worth more to finance than a marginal rate saving.

body.h3: 5. What happens when the plan changes

body.p: Ask what the notice period is to extend and to leave early, and get the answer before you book rather than after the dates move. Hotels are usually more flexible night to night; apartments are usually cheaper if the stay holds. The risk is priced differently in each.

body.h2: Where hotels still win outright

body.p: Short trips, obviously. Anything where the traveller arrives late and leaves early. Anywhere a twenty-four-hour desk genuinely matters — an unfamiliar city, a late inbound flight, a traveller who would rather not be troubleshooting a building entry system at midnight. Group travel where everyone needs to be under one roof for a meeting the next morning. And any market where you have negotiated hotel rates good enough to move the crossover point out.
None of that is an argument against apartments. It is an argument against having a single default.

body.h2: Running the comparison in practice

list: Pull one real trip of each type from the last quarter and cost it both ways, fully loaded. It takes an hour and it settles most internal arguments.
Set a length threshold in policy, then allow exceptions rather than requiring approval for the sensible option. If the policy makes the cheaper format harder to book, people will not book it.
Check what “serviced” means per operator: housekeeping frequency, linen, whether utilities are capped, and who answers at nine on a Sunday evening.
Confirm accountability. A directly contracted operator with a named contact behaves differently from a listing on a consumer site when something goes wrong.
Review it annually. Rates move, supply moves, and your travel pattern moves. A threshold set three years ago is a guess about a different market.

body.h2: The short version

body.p: Treat hotels and serviced apartments as two tools rather than two camps. Below roughly a week, a hotel usually wins on convenience and often on total cost. Past a couple of weeks the apartment usually wins on both, and the gap widens the longer the stay runs. The programmes that get this right are not the ones with the strongest opinion — they are the ones that can source either format at a sensible rate in the city the work is actually in, and that decide per stay.

title: What Does a Corporate Travel Management Company Actually Do?
excerpt: Not a booking site, and not only a ticketing agency. What a TMC actually covers, how it differs from booking in-house, and how to tell whether your company has outgrown managing travel informally.
meta: Corporate travel management explained: what a TMC does, how it differs from booking in-house, and what to ask before you appoint one.

body.p: “Travel management company” is a term the industry uses freely and buyers rarely have a precise definition for. It is not a booking site, and it is not only an agency that issues tickets. This is what a corporate travel management company does, what it does not do, and how to tell whether your company is at the point of needing one.

body.h2: The short answer

body.p: A travel management company runs a company’s travel programme as a service: sourcing and negotiating accommodation and transport, providing the channel people book through, supporting travellers while they are away, and returning the spend to finance as something that can be reconciled and analysed. A booking site sells you a trip. A TMC manages the fact that your organisation takes hundreds of them. The scope varies by provider — our own corporate travel services page sets out how those pieces are usually divided.

body.h2: What a TMC does, in practice

body.h3: Sourcing and negotiating

body.p: Aggregating a company’s demand and taking it to suppliers — hotels, serviced apartment operators, ground transport fleets — to secure rates and terms an individual booker would not get. The value is not only the discount; it is the terms around it, such as cancellation flexibility, inclusive breakfast or wifi, and guaranteed availability in cities where the company travels predictably.

body.h3: Booking and approval

body.p: Providing the channel bookings run through, whether that is a team that books on request, a self-booking tool, or both. Policy is enforced here rather than after the fact — in-policy options shown first, out-of-policy choices routed for approval automatically instead of by email.

body.h3: Support while people are travelling

body.p: A cancelled flight at eleven at night is the moment a programme is actually tested. Support means someone reachable who can rebook, rearrange the onward transfer and tell the company where its traveller is. This is also the duty-of-care function, and it depends on the bookings having gone through the channel in the first place.

body.h3: Billing, reporting and reconciliation

body.p: Consolidating what would otherwise be hundreds of individual charges into billing finance can allocate, and turning the underlying data into something a travel manager can act on — spend by cost centre, by supplier, by city, advance booking windows, policy compliance.

body.h3: Everything that is not a flight or a hotel

body.p: The larger providers cover ground transport, MICE and event travel, group movements, and employee relocation. Whether a company needs all of that from one place depends on how much of it it does — but there is a real coordination benefit when the same team handles a relocation’s flights, temporary accommodation and household goods.

body.h2: TMC, booking site, or in-house?

body.p: A consumer booking site is excellent at one transaction. It has no view of your policy, no negotiated position on your behalf, no consolidated invoice and no obligation to you at two in the morning. For a company taking a handful of trips a year, that is fine.

Doing it in-house means someone — usually an office manager or an EA — absorbs the sourcing, booking and problem-solving alongside their actual job. This scales further than people expect and then stops abruptly, normally when travel volume becomes unpredictable or the company starts operating in cities nobody in the office knows.

A TMC makes sense once the programme is large enough that someone would otherwise be managing it full time, or once the consequences of getting it wrong — a stranded traveller, an unbudgeted quarter, an audit nobody can answer — have become material.

body.h2: Where the technology fits

body.p: Most TMCs now put a self-booking tool in front of the service, so routine trips are booked by the traveller inside policy while the team handles the complicated ones. That combination matters more than either half: a tool with no support behind it fails at exactly the moments support is needed, and a service with no tool makes a simple domestic booking take three emails.
Our own platform, Travgenie, is built on that principle — policy-aligned booking and automated approvals for the routine, with the desks still there for everything else.

body.h2: What to ask before appointing one

list: Which of these functions are actually included, and which are priced separately. Scope varies far more between providers than pricing does.
How support works out of hours — a named team, a shared inbox, or a call centre — and what the realistic response time is.
What the reporting looks like. Ask to see a real report rather than a description of one.
How they are paid — transaction fee, management fee, supplier commission, or a mix. It shapes their incentives.
Whether they hold the supplier relationships directly in the markets that matter to you, or source them through someone else.
How they handle the long tail: relocations, group movements, one-off events.

body.h2: Is your company ready for one?

body.p: A rough test: if you cannot answer how much the company spent on travel last year, where your travellers are this week, or what proportion of bookings followed policy — and if those questions matter to somebody — then the programme has outgrown being managed informally. That is the point at which a TMC starts paying for itself, usually in reclaimed time before it shows up in rates.

title: What Is a Corporate Travel Policy (and Why Your Company Needs One)
excerpt: A travel policy answers "what can I spend on a hotel?" without a conversation. What belongs in one, the two ways they fail, and why compliance is a design problem rather than a discipline problem.
meta: A travel policy answers "what can I spend on a hotel?" without a conversation. What belongs in one, the two ways they fail, and why compliance is a…

body.p: Plenty of companies run travel without a written policy. It works, roughly, while the company is small enough that everyone books the same way for the same reasons. It stops working at the point where nobody can answer a simple question — what are we allowed to spend on a hotel in Bengaluru? — without asking someone. A travel policy is the document that answers that without a conversation.

body.h2: What a travel policy actually is

body.p: It is a short set of rules covering who can travel, how they book, what they can spend, and what the company does if something goes wrong. It is not a procurement document and it is not a legal one. Its job is to let a person book a trip correctly without asking permission, and to let finance approve the result without an investigation.

It sits alongside whoever runs the programme in practice. If you are still working out what that division of labour looks like, our overview of corporate travel services sets out which parts a travel partner typically takes on and which stay in-house.

body.h2: What belongs in one

body.h3: Scope: who and when

body.p: Which employees it covers, whether contractors and candidates are included, and what counts as business travel. Ambiguity here is where most disputes start — a trip that is half conference and half holiday needs a rule written before someone books it, not after.

body.h3: Booking channel and approval

body.p: Where trips are booked and who signs off. The single most useful line in most policies is the one that says all travel is booked through one channel. It is what makes everything downstream — rates, reporting, duty of care — actually possible. Approval thresholds should be set so that routine trips do not need a signature and unusual ones do.

body.h3: Accommodation standards

body.p: A caps-by-city approach ages better than a star rating, because a four-star property means very different things in different markets. Say what the cap is, say it is inclusive or exclusive of tax, and say what happens when there is genuinely nothing available underneath it. Include a line on longer stays, where a serviced apartment is often the cheaper unit.

body.h3: Ground transport

body.p: When a chauffeur-driven car is appropriate, when a taxi or ride-hailing app is, and whether self-drive hire is permitted at all. Late-night airport transfers are worth naming explicitly — this is a safety clause disguised as a spend clause.

body.h3: Expenses: what is in and what is not

body.p: Meals, laundry on longer trips, connectivity, tips, and the personal spend that is not reimbursable. A short list of what is not covered prevents more argument than a long list of what is.

body.h3: Duty of care

body.p: What the company will do if a traveller is ill, delayed, or somewhere that becomes unsafe, and who they call. This is the section people skip and the one that matters most on the day it is needed. It also depends entirely on the company knowing where its travellers are — which, again, requires the single booking channel.

body.h2: The two ways policies fail

body.h3: Too vague to follow

body.p: “Book reasonably” is not a rule. It puts the judgement on the traveller, produces wildly inconsistent spend, and gives finance nothing to enforce. If a policy cannot answer the Bengaluru hotel question in one line, it will be ignored.

body.h3: Too strict to follow

body.p: The opposite failure is more common and less obvious. A policy that requires three quotes for a domestic flight, or approval from someone two levels up for a routine trip, does not reduce spend — it moves bookings outside the channel. People book on a consumer site, expense it, and the programme loses the rate, the data and the ability to find anyone in a crisis. That costs far more than the exception would have.

body.h2: Compliance is a design problem

body.p: The instinct when compliance is poor is to add enforcement. It is usually the wrong lever. People book out of policy overwhelmingly because the compliant route was slower, harder or produced a worse trip — not because they were trying to.

The fix is nearly always to make the compliant path the easy one: a booking tool that shows only in-policy options by default, approvals that route automatically instead of by email, and a human to call when the tool cannot help. When the path of least resistance is also the compliant one, compliance stops needing to be policed.

body.h2: How to tell whether it is working

list: Channel share — what proportion of trips came through the official route. This is the number that makes every other number trustworthy.
Advance booking window — how far ahead people book. It moves before cost does, so it is an early signal.
Exception volume and type — a steady stream of the same exception is not indiscipline, it is a policy line that does not match how the business works.
Time to book — if a routine trip takes half an hour to arrange, the policy is costing salary to save on rates.

body.h2: Where to start

body.p: Two pages. Scope, booking channel, approval, accommodation caps, ground transport, expenses, duty of care, and who to contact. Write it against how the company actually travels now rather than how you would like it to, publish it somewhere people will find it, and review it once a year with whoever books the most trips in the room. A short policy that is followed beats a thorough one that is not.

title: What Are Serviced Apartments — and Why Corporates Are Choosing Them
excerpt: A serviced apartment is a fully equipped home let on hotel-like terms. For travel programmes managing assignments measured in weeks rather than nights, it is often the more sensible unit of accommodation — and the reasons are practical, not fashionable.
meta: A serviced apartment is a fully equipped home let on hotel-like terms. What it includes, when it beats a hotel for business travel, and what to check.

body.p: Ask a travel manager what changed in their accommodation mix over the last few years and the serviced apartment usually comes up. Not as a trend — as a line that quietly grew because the maths kept pointing at it. Here is what the format actually is, where it earns its place in a corporate programme, and where a hotel is still the better answer.

body.h2: What a serviced apartment actually is

body.p: A serviced apartment is a self-contained home — bedroom, living area, an equipped kitchen, usually a washing machine — let on flexible terms with housekeeping, utilities, internet and building security folded into one rate. The distinction that matters is not luxury. It is structure: you are booking a home that is serviced, rather than a room that is staffed.

The formats vary more than the label suggests. Aparthotels sit inside a managed building with a reception desk and look much like a hotel from the lobby. Corporate housing tends to be a residential apartment in a residential block, taken for months at a time. Extended-stay brands sit between the two. All three trade as serviced apartments, and which one suits an assignment depends on how long it runs and how much front desk the traveller genuinely needs.

body.h2: Why corporate travel teams are moving toward them

body.p: Three things drive it, and none of them is novelty.

body.h3: The economics change past about a week

body.p: Hotel rates are quoted per night and priced for one or two people who eat out. An apartment is priced for a longer let and comes with a kitchen, so the daily rate is typically lower and the incidental spend — breakfasts, laundry, dinners on expenses — falls with it. The longer the stay, the wider the gap. For a short trip the difference is noise; for a twelve-week deployment it is a budget line.

body.h3: One line item instead of several

body.p: Utilities, internet, housekeeping and often parking sit inside a single rate. That makes an assignment easier to budget before it starts and easier to reconcile after it ends. For a finance team, one predictable invoice covering a three-month posting is usually worth more than a marginally cheaper nightly rate that arrives as ninety separate charges across two quarters.

body.h3: People do better in them

body.p: This is the least measurable reason and often the one that matters most. Somebody on a long project who can cook, do their own laundry, have a colleague round and keep something resembling a routine finishes the assignment in better shape than somebody living out of a suitcase in a room with a kettle. Attrition on long deployments carries a real cost, and accommodation is one of the few levers a travel programme can actually pull on it.

body.h2: Where they fit — and where they do not

body.p: Serviced apartments are strongest for extended assignments, project deployments, relocations, and the settling-in period before an employee finds permanent housing. They also work well for small teams travelling together: a two- or three-bedroom unit frequently costs less than the equivalent hotel rooms and gives the group somewhere to work in the evening.

They are usually the wrong answer for a one- or two-night trip. Check-in can be less flexible, there is not always a twenty-four-hour desk, and the things that make an apartment good over six weeks — space, a kitchen, a residential location — buy you very little over two nights. A well-run programme uses both and decides per stay, not per policy.

body.h2: What to check before you book one

list: Location against the actual place of work, not the city centre. An apartment fifteen minutes from the office is worth more to the traveller than a fashionable postcode forty minutes away.
What “serviced” includes. Housekeeping frequency, linen changes, whether utilities are capped, and what happens if something breaks at nine on a Sunday evening.
Minimum stay, and the notice to extend or leave early. Assignments move. The contract should be able to move with them.
Who is accountable. A directly contracted operator with a named contact is a different proposition from a listing on a consumer booking site.
How it invoices. If the programme runs on cost-centre allocation or centralised billing, confirm that before the booking rather than after the first invoice.

body.h2: The short version

body.p: For anything longer than about a week, a serviced apartment is usually cheaper to run, easier to account for, and better for the person staying in it. For anything shorter, a hotel generally still wins. The useful discipline is to treat the two as different tools rather than as a house preference — and to have someone in the programme who can secure either, at a negotiated rate, in the city the work is actually in.
If you would like to see how that plays out across your own travel pattern, our serviced apartments desk will come back with costed options rather than a brochure.
